uncited: This method decomposes a composite radiance field into individual object layers and distinct background layers (near and far) to enable per-object editing and re-rendering.

*   **Inputs:** A trained hybrid voxel-MLP model (from [Object-NeRF](11987-object-nerf.md)), 3D bounding boxes for each object in the scene (obtained from a detector), and camera ray parameters $(\mathbf{o}, \mathbf{d})$.
*   **Outputs:** Decomposed color $\mathbf{c}$ and opacity $\alpha$ for individual objects, near background, and far background.
*   **3D Bounding Boxes:** Axis-aligned or oriented boxes defining the spatial extent of each object $i$.
**Ray Partitioning:** For a given ray, determine which segments intersect the 3D bounding boxes of the objects.
**Far Background Rendering:** For ray segments outside all object bounding boxes, query the standard scene MLP to retrieve color $\mathbf{c}^b_i$ and density $\sigma^b_i$.
**Near Background Rendering:** To isolate the near background, prune rays inside the object bounding boxes.
This is achieved by setting the density $\sigma^{nb}_i$ to a large negative value ($-1 \times 10^{-5}$) before volumetric rendering.
**Object Rendering:** For each object $i$, restrict sampling to the interior of its 3D bounding box.
**Compositing:** Aggregate the contributions from far background ($b$), near background ($nb$), and objects ($o$) using alpha compositing weights $w$.
Where $w^b_i, w^{nb}_i, w^o_i$ are the accumulated weights for the far background, near background, and object $i$ respectively along the ray.
*   **No Objectness Prior:** The decomposition is purely learned from multi-view image-based rendering.
*   **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of objects and the resolution of the feature grid.
Requires additional ray-box intersection tests and separate integration passes for far background, near background, and each object.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing 3D bounding boxes for all objects.
The feature grid size is determined by the parent Object-NeRF model.
Provides full control over object editability.
Artifacts may appear in regions with no overlap in sparse views.
It builds upon the Object-NeRF framework to address few-shot novel view synthesis and scene decomposition tasks.
